tests.summary_sentence: The automated test suite (654 tests) passed 653; the single failure is a concurrency test showing that two simultaneous duplicate alert ingests lose one occurrence count.
tests.row: 653 passed, 1 failed (tests/alerts/test_alert_occurrence_count_race.py: occurrence_count 2 instead of 3 after concurrent duplicate ingests, a lost-update race). Run with 4 parallel workers (pytest -n 4, SQLite test database, 1 h 50 min); line coverage 44%.

install_steps: Created VM 106 from the Ubuntu 24.04 cloud image with cloud-init (SSH key, DHCP) and updated the system.
qm create 106 … ; qm set 106 --scsi0 local-thin-storage:0,import-from=noble-server-cloudimg-amd64.img ; apt full-upgrade
Installed PostgreSQL 16 and Valkey; created the database and role; set a Valkey password.
apt install postgresql valkey-server ; CREATE USER flowintel … ; CREATE DATABASE flowintel OWNER flowintel
Cloned the repository and copied the default configuration files.
git clone https://github.com/flowintel/flowintel ; cp conf/config.py.default conf/config.py ; cp conf/config_module.py.default conf/config_module.py
Exported the configuration as environment variables (SECRET_KEY, DB_*, VALKEY_*, FLOWINTEL_APP_HOST=0.0.0.0).

Ran the official installer: system packages, pandoc, Node/nvm, Mermaid CLI, Python venv (uv), Bun assets, git submodules, database initialisation, taxonomies, galaxies, MISP modules and default cases.
./launch.sh -l   (Flask, misp-modules, notification and MISP-sync workers in screen sessions)
Loaded the bundled community test data through the API.
Installed the development requirements and ran the automated test suite.
uv pip install -r requirements-dev.txt ; FLOWINTEL_APP_ENV=testing python -m pytest -n 4 -p no:randomly --cov=./app
install_issues: misp__attribute.value is VARCHAR(255). Any IoC value longer than 255 characters makes POST /api/case/create_with_event fail with HTTP 500 (StringDataRightTruncation on PostgreSQL). Because every attribute is committed separately, the case remains in the database half-imported. 3,530 cases (MISP events and CSV/free-text chunks) were affected; 338,907 IoCs (9.6%) were missing.

Critical for TI imports. Test workaround: column changed to TEXT, the B-tree index on value replaced by a hash index, incomplete cases deleted and re-created through the API (3,530 cases). Afterwards 0 differences against the sources. SQLite does not enforce the length, so the problem only appears with PostgreSQL/MariaDB.
MISP object-level first_seen/last_seen are not stored (table case__misp__object has no date columns).
Date information lost for objects, e.g. all 1,801 dated objects of NOCACTI Intrusion and 859 of Rectifyq 2026. Not worked around.

Bulk import is slow: one INSERT + COMMIT + SELECT of the case per attribute, about 90 IoCs/s per application process (database initialisation of taxonomies and galaxies took about 35 minutes for the same reason).

Test workaround: PostgreSQL synchronous_commit=off and four extra application processes on ports 7007–7010 sharing the database (about 290 IoCs/s). The full import of 3.5 million IoCs took about 3 hours.
No index on misp__attribute.case_misp_object_id.
Deleting cases/objects scans the whole attribute table. Index added for the test.
install.sh installs only requirements.txt, so ./launch.sh -t fails with 'No module named pytest'.
Installed requirements-dev.txt.

launch.sh uses the shebang '#!/bin/bash -i' (interactive shell) and therefore reads ~/.bashrc. With DB_* variables exported from .bashrc the test suite connects to PostgreSQL ('database flowintel_test_master does not exist') and every test errors at setup.
Configuration removed from .bashrc for the test run. The '_test_' name guard in tests/conftest.py prevents the production database from being dropped, but the behaviour is fragile.
Test suite: test_concurrent_duplicate_ingests_count_every_occurrence fails (occurrence_count 2, expected 3).
Concurrent ingests of the same alert can lose an occurrence count (lost update). Minor for this analysis; worth reporting upstream.
install.sh runs 'nvm install node 20.19.2', which installs the latest Node.js (26.13.0), not 20.19.2.
No functional impact seen; Node version not pinned as intended.
The development launch runs Flask in DEBUG mode with the Werkzeug debugger; with FLOWINTEL_APP_HOST=0.0.0.0 it is reachable from the network.
Acceptable only on an isolated test network (here NAT behind the Proxmox host). Use ./launch.sh -p with gunicorn behind nginx for real use.
Application processes grew to about 1.4 GB RAM each during the bulk import.
Observation; the 8 GB VM was sufficient.
'apt install valkey' in install.sh resolves to valkey-server on Ubuntu 24.04.
No issue.

findings: Only a minority of TI sources provide IoC lifetimes

Of the 14 usable MISP-format sources, only the two NOCACTI feeds give both first_seen and last_seen for every IoC. Infoblox gives a start date for every IoC (2021-01-01 to 2026-10-15) but no end date. Four sources (Rösti, PrecisionSec, TweetFeed, SiberKapan; 631,295 IoCs) give no attribute dates at all.

Across all MISP-format sources only 1.1% of IoCs have both dates. Statistical work on IoC lifetime is therefore possible only for a few sources, and the results are dominated by NOCACTI and Rectifyq 2026.
Dates describe very different things per source

NOCACTI Intrusion: median lifetime 0.01 days (about 15 minutes) – a single sighting. NOCACTI Adversary Infrastructure: median 39 days, P90 330 days – infrastructure activity. CIRCL OSINT: median 44 days. Rectifyq 2026: median 0.05 days but a long tail up to 18 years (6,671 days).

CIRCL OSINT has last_seen on 51% of IoCs but almost always without first_seen; these come from 288 daily 'Maltrail IOC for <date>' events where last_seen is the publication day. Counting 'end dates' without checking their origin would overstate the available lifetime information.

None of the 1.57 million CSV/free-text IoCs has a date in Flowintel, even though most lines of the dataplane.org, abuse.ch SSLBL, James Brine, Feodo, ipspamlist, MalSilo and Phishtank feeds contain dates. This follows MISP's feed model (values only), not a Flowintel defect, but it means most IP/domain reputation data enters without any temporal information.

The 255-character limit on attribute values combined with per-attribute commits causes failed and half-imported cases on PostgreSQL. In this test it silently removed 9.6% of the IoCs, including dated ones, until it was worked around.
Object-level first_seen/last_seen are discarded. The bulk import path is slow (about 90 IoCs/s per process).
recommendations: Report to the Flowintel project: change misp__attribute.value to TEXT (with a hash or expression index), wrap create_with_event in a single transaction so that a failure does not leave partial cases, and store object-level first_seen/last_seen.

For TI work with Flowintel, prefer sources that provide attribute first_seen/last_seen (NOCACTI, Infoblox for start dates, Rectifyq 2026, CIRCL for selected events) and document what each source's dates mean.

If temporal analysis of reputation feeds is needed, add a custom import that maps the date columns of CSV feeds (dataplane.org, abuse.ch, Feodo, ipspamlist, MalSilo, Phishtank) to first_seen/last_seen.
For bulk imports, batch attribute inserts in Flowintel or import through MISP and sync, and plan for several hours per million IoCs with the current code.
Run Flowintel in production mode (./launch.sh -p, gunicorn behind nginx with TLS); do not expose the development server.
Add requirements-dev.txt to the documented test procedure and avoid relying on an interactive shell in launch.sh.
limitations: Snapshot of 29 October 2026: feed contents change daily; CSV/free-text feeds in particular contain only current entries.
29 catalogue entries are not analysed: 25 could not be downloaded (gone, forbidden, timeout) and 4 returned an HTML page or empty content; some may work with registration or from another network.

CSV/free-text parsing re-implements MISP's rules (value columns, delimiters, exclusion regex, free-text type detection); small differences in type detection compared with MISP are possible. Duplicate IoCs within a source were removed.
Dates were analysed as stored in attribute first_seen/last_seen. Dates in event metadata, object-level fields, object attributes or comments are reported in table 6.3 but not used as IoC dates.
The schema workaround (TEXT column, hash index, extra index, synchronous_commit=off) changes the tested system; figures for the unmodified schema are given in section 6.4.
The development launch mode was used; production mode (gunicorn) was not tested.
